title: Financial caution is reallocating discretionary life rather than stopping consumption: households cut everyday room and large purchases while preserving selected food, leisure, culture, and resale occasions
source_unit: KPMG UK, Consumer Pulse Q3 2026: Consumer confidence marginally improves, heading toward final quarter of 2026
geography: United Kingdom consumer households, with quarterly comparison and September 2026 outlook

observations.period: September 2-9, 2026; financial security and perceived economic direction

denominator.unit: UK consumers surveyed online by OnePoll for KPMG UK

financially_secure.unit: percent describing themselves as financially secure

financially_insecure.unit: percent describing themselves as financially insecure

economy_worsening.unit: percent saying the UK economy is worsening

economy_improving.unit: percent saying the UK economy is improving

perceived_cost_pressures.value: among those seeing the economy as worsening, groceries, utilities, and eating or drinking out were the most cited reasons

observations.method: KPMG Consumer Pulse survey conducted online by OnePoll among 3,000 UK consumers from 2-9 September 2026; the release reports quarter-over-quarter comparisons and descriptive associations.
observations.uncertainty: This is an online sponsor-commissioned survey and does not establish population-level causal effects, verified household budgets, realized financial resilience, or representative behavior for every UK subgroup.
observations.subgroup: UK consumers differentiated by perceived financial security, economic outlook, age, and spending situation in the published tables.
observations.counterinterpretation: Perceived security and economic direction can diverge because people evaluate their own finances, public services, and national economy through different reference points; seasonal spending also matters.

observations.period: September 2026; adaptation responses among consumers who see the economy worsening

denominator.unit: respondents in the KPMG sample reporting that the economy is worsening

reduce_everyday_spending.unit: percent reporting that they reduce monthly spending on everyday items as a precaution

save_more.unit: percent reporting that they save more as a contingency

defer_big_ticket.unit: percent reporting that they defer big-ticket purchases

employment_stickiness.unit: percent reporting they are less inclined to leave their current employment

adaptation_route.value: economic pessimism converts into precautionary spending, savings, purchase timing, and job-mobility decisions

observations.method: Descriptive follow-up questions asked of respondents who said the economy was worsening; multiple responses could be selected.
observations.uncertainty: The data do not show the size or duration of spending reductions, whether saving is feasible, or whether job stickiness reflects security, fear, satisfaction, or limited alternatives.
observations.subgroup: UK consumers reporting a worsening economy, with household room and employment decisions observed through self-report.
observations.counterinterpretation: Precautionary saving can improve future resilience, and reduced job mobility can be temporary seasonal caution rather than durable labor-market constraint.

observations.period: June-August 2026; reported food, leisure, cultural, and appearance spending

restaurant.unit: percent reporting eating at a restaurant in the previous three months

takeaway.unit: percent reporting ordering takeaway food at home

cinema.unit: percent reporting going to the cinema

ticketed_event.unit: percent reporting attending a gig, theatre, or other ticketed event

selected_occasions.value: continued social, food, leisure, and appearance spending coexists with caution about essentials and large purchases

observations.method: Self-reported three-month activity in the KPMG Consumer Pulse survey; categories are not mutually exclusive and do not measure spending amounts.
observations.uncertainty: Participation shares do not establish frequency, price, household budget impact, affordability, or whether activities were traded down, subsidized, or financed.
observations.subgroup: UK consumers overall, with differences by financial security and consumer circumstances available in the survey instrument and published release.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reported participation can remain high while frequency, quality, venue choice, or spending per occasion falls; social and cultural occasions may be treated as high-value forms of connection.

observations.period: June-August 2026; resale, channels, payments, and future big-ticket plans

resale.unit: percent reporting selling clothing or footwear on a resale site

no_big_ticket_purchase.unit: percent reporting no big-ticket purchase in the previous three months

no_future_big_ticket_plan.unit: percent reporting no planned big-ticket spending in the following three months

resale_and_channel_route.value: financial caution coexists with channel hybridity and resale participation, while large-purchase optionality remains compressed

observations.method: Descriptive self-reported purchase, resale, payment, channel, and future-intention questions in the KPMG Consumer Pulse survey.
observations.uncertainty: The release does not identify transaction values, profitability of resale, debt exposure, household-level substitution, or whether planned purchases occur.
observations.subgroup: UK consumers, with resale highest among 18-24-year-olds for selling clothing or footwear in the reported data.
observations.counterinterpretation: Resale can reflect fashion, sustainability, or identity as well as financial pressure; in-store and online shares overlap and do not reveal channel loyalty or retailer outcomes.

related_sources.claim: Official KPMG UK release with sample, field dates, security, economic outlook, spending, channel, resale, and future-intention results.

boundary: This record adds a current UK consumer-behavior route from financial security and perceived economic decline through precautionary spending, job stickiness, social and cultural occasions, resale, channels, and big-ticket optionality. It is a sponsor-commissioned online survey and descriptive pulse, not verified transaction data, household-budget microdata, a causal consumption model, or a universal consumer trend.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official KPMG UK release reviewed for OnePoll sample and field dates, financial-security categories, economic concerns, precautionary responses, spending occasions, resale, channels, payments, and big-ticket plans.
